info.title: Canopy gRPC API
info.description: Companion contract for Canopy's gRPC API and its private Nginx streaming authorization endpoint. The /canopy.* entries describe gRPC methods for API discovery; Canopy does not expose them as a separate REST API. Protobuf remains the canonical contract.

tags.name: Playback
tags.description: Anonymous-capable playback control and stream resolution.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Native identity, account lifecycle, external identity linking, and device sessions.

post.description: Creates a pending native account. Stores only password hashes and challenge-token digests; queues verification email payload after persistence. Registration throttling may return RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED.
Rotates a pending-account verification challenge when eligible. Public response remains generic for missing, active, disabled, deleted, and throttled accounts.
Atomically consumes a single-use email verification challenge, activates the account, creates the profile, and returns access and refresh tokens.
Authenticates an active native account and creates a device session. Failed attempts are rate limited by hashed normalized email.
Creates a password-reset challenge for active native accounts when eligible. Public response remains generic for missing, inactive, and throttled accounts.
Atomically consumes a reset challenge, writes the new password hash, and revokes sessions for the account.
Requires native identity metadata. Rechecks the session, verifies the current password, writes the new hash, and revokes other sessions according to server policy.
Creates a one-time Google OIDC nonce challenge. The server stores only a nonce digest plus internal challenge payload.

Consumes the nonce challenge, verifies the Google ID token and nonce, keys identity by Google sub, and returns either a session or explicit account-link-required challenge. Email equality alone never links accounts.

412.description: FAILED_PRECONDITION when Google OIDC verification is not configured

post.description: Requires native identity metadata and an explicit link challenge produced by CompleteGoogleLogin. The challenge is consumed atomically before attaching the Google sub.

200.description: Linked or already linked to this account.

412.description: FAILED_PRECONDITION when the Google sub belongs to another account

post.description: Requires native identity metadata. Idempotently removes the account's Google external identity.
Transactionally rotates a refresh token. Reuse of a consumed refresh token revokes the session family and records a hashed abuse signal.
Requires native identity metadata. Idempotently revokes the current session and consumes outstanding refresh tokens.
Requires native identity metadata. Idempotently revokes all account sessions and consumes outstanding refresh tokens.
Requires native identity metadata. Lists device sessions scoped to the authenticated account.
Requires native identity metadata. Idempotently revokes one account-owned session.
Requires native identity metadata. Returns the authenticated account summary.
Requires native identity metadata. Idempotently marks the account deleted, revokes sessions immediately, and purges delegated profile-owned state according to Canopy policy.

get.description: Infrastructure-only endpoint on the private listener. Clients must use ResolvePlayback and never call this endpoint directly. Public capabilities recheck release-safe readiness; personal capabilities recheck personal readiness and require the asset owner to remain the currently configured instance owner.

204.description: Authorized; Nginx receives internal redirect metadata.

403.description: Generic denial for missing, malformed, expired, revoked, or unknown capabilities.

post.description: Accepts optional gRPC authentication metadata and returns a short-lived Canopy stream capability URL served through Nginx. Anonymous and authenticated non-owner callers resolve release-safe ready media only. The configured owner resolves owner-scoped personal ready media first, with public fallback. Invalid supplied credentials are unauthenticated; inaccessible personal media is indistinguishable from missing media.

401.description: Authentication metadata was supplied but is malformed, expired, or invalid.

404.description: No eligible media is visible to the caller. Missing and inaccessible personal media use the same response.

post.description: Returns the next shuffle-channel track after applying recent-play exclusion and diversity rules.

x-canopy-docs.persistenceStatus: PostgreSQL provider ingest is transactional and idempotent by provider identity; discovery materialization uses one representative asset per track.
x-canopy-docs.sessionControlStatus: PandaEngine owns playback control and queue/session state. Canonical canopy.v1 playback RPCs resolve authorized playback sources only; prototype session-control projections are noncanonical legacy documentation until the companion is fully regenerated.
x-canopy-docs.providerFixtureStartup: Set CANOPY_PROVIDER_FIXTURE_PATH in PostgreSQL mode to ingest a local ProviderTrack fixture before serving gRPC.
x-canopy-docs.healthStatus: Health responses include aggregate status plus dependency details. PostgreSQL and managed local media are the active readiness dependencies.
x-canopy-docs.authModel: Anonymous users may browse, search, and play, but anonymous sessions are not durable users and receive no backend history, library, likes, preferences, playlists, or durable sessions. AuthService owns native identity, password reset/change, Google login/linking, account lifecycle, and device sessions. Durable state RPCs in the bounded canopy.v1 services require native identity metadata authorization: Bearer <identity access token>; Canopy verifies the Ed25519 access token and rechecks session state before resolving profiles. Auth abuse controls use hashed fixed-window buckets; registration and password-login throttles may surface RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, while generic verification-resend and password-reset requests remain accepted when throttled.
x-canopy-docs.playbackResolution: ResolvePlayback accepts track_id, optional session_id, and optional gRPC auth metadata. The configured owner receives owner-scoped personal media first with public fallback; anonymous and non-owner callers receive release-safe public media only. Invalid supplied auth is rejected, inaccessible personal media is concealed as not found, and successful resolution loads the track into the session.
x-canopy-docs.storageModel: Active playback uses Canopy-managed local media authorized by Canopy and served through Nginx. No external catalog or object-storage provider is wired into the runtime; RustFS remains optional Compose infrastructure only.
x-canopy-docs.profileStatus: UpsertProfile requires native identity metadata, resolves the authenticated account/profile scope, and stores history_enabled as the logged-in user history preference.
x-canopy-docs.historyStatus: Playback history is an append-only profile-owned event ledger. Lifecycle RPCs require metadata auth. Disabling history atomically and irreversibly purges existing events, and consent-safe recording prevents concurrent repopulation. Anonymous sessions never create or read backend history.
x-canopy-docs.libraryStatus: Library RPCs require native identity metadata auth and persist profile-owned saved tracks only for logged-in users. Saved-track list resources include TrackSummary plus saved_at relationship metadata.
x-canopy-docs.likesStatus: Like RPCs require native identity metadata auth and persist profile-owned positive track likes only for logged-in users. Liked-track list resources include TrackSummary plus liked_at relationship metadata.
x-canopy-docs.preferencesStatus: Preference RPCs require native identity metadata auth and store a profile-owned JSON object; anonymous client preferences remain client-side.
x-canopy-docs.playlistStatus: Playlist RPCs require native identity metadata auth and an existing profile. Private playlists and ordered track memberships persist under profiles.id; anonymous sessions never create playlist rows. AddPlaylistTrack returns PlaylistTrack, ReorderPlaylistTracks returns Playlist, and playlist-track list resources include position and added_at relationship metadata.
x-canopy-docs.contractModel: Protobuf is the canonical RPC contract. This OpenAPI document is a human- and tooling-friendly companion for the gRPC methods plus the private HTTP stream-authorization boundary; it does not imply REST transcoding or replace Buf-generated protobuf documentation.
x-canopy-docs.collectionStatus: Saved-track, liked-track, and playlist-track list responses use resource shapes that include both renderable TrackSummary data and relationship metadata such as saved_at, liked_at, position, and added_at.
